questions.question: Uses packet switching technology to carry voice traffic over an IP network where each packet follows the best path to reach its destination.

correct_answer_points: VoIP means Voice over Internet Protocol.
It carries voice as IP packets rather than traditional circuit-switched calls.
Packet routing can choose paths dynamically across the IP network.
Email, HTTP and SMTP are not voice-over-IP technologies.

options.a: Email is used mainly for asynchronous electronic messages; it does not carry voice as IP packets.
options.b: HTTP is a web communication protocol used to transfer web resources; it is not a voice-calling technology.
options.d: SMTP is used to send email between mail systems; it does not provide VoIP voice transport.

questions.question: Which of the following refers to the level of data abstraction that describes how data is actually stored?

correct_answer_points: Physical-level abstraction describes how data is physically stored.
It deals with storage structures, files, blocks and physical organization.
Conceptual and logical levels describe what data means and how users view it.
Remember: physical level = actual storage details.

options.a: The conceptual level describes the overall logical structure of the database; it does not describe physical storage details.
options.c: File level is not the standard ANSI/SPARC abstraction level for describing how database data is physically stored.
options.d: The logical/conceptual view describes what data is stored and relationships, not the actual storage structures.

questions.question: How can you make an asynchronous request to a server in JavaScript?

correct_answer_points: Fetch and XMLHttpRequest can initiate asynchronous HTTP/network requests.
They let JavaScript continue executing while the request is in progress.
The async and await keywords control Promise-based code but do not themselves perform the network request.
A callback can handle asynchronous results, but the most direct option given is Fetch/XHR.

options.a: async marks a function as returning a Promise; it does not itself send an HTTP request.
options.b: await waits for a Promise result; it is not the API that creates the server request.
options.d: A callback can handle an asynchronous result, but the question asks how to make the server request itself.

questions.question: Which Internet protocol is responsible for mapping IP addresses to MAC addresses?

correct_answer_points: ARP stands for Address Resolution Protocol.
It maps an IPv4 address to the MAC address of a device on the local network.
TCP provides reliable transport; ICMP carries control/error messages.
DNS maps domain names to IP addresses, not IP addresses to MAC addresses.

options.b: TCP provides reliable transport between endpoints; it does not resolve an IPv4 address to a MAC address.
options.c: ICMP carries network control and error messages; it is not used for IPv4-to-MAC resolution.
options.d: DNS maps domain names to IP addresses; it does not normally map IP addresses to MAC addresses.

questions.question: Inter-Process Communication (IPC) is a mechanism used for:
options: (b) Allowing processes to run independently without communication
(c) Enabling processes to exchange information and synchronize their tasks
(d) Enabling processes to execute in a random order
questions.correct_answer: Enabling processes to exchange information and synchronize their tasks

correct_answer_points: IPC lets processes communicate with one another.
It supports data exchange and synchronization between processes.
Common IPC mechanisms include pipes, shared memory, message queues and sockets.
Its purpose is communication, not preventing concurrency or random execution.

options.a: IPC is not intended to stop concurrent execution; it lets concurrent processes coordinate when needed.
options.b: Processes may run independently, but IPC specifically exists when they need to exchange data or synchronize.
options.d: IPC does not define a random execution order; scheduling and synchronization determine execution behavior.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Type 1 language or Type 1 grammar?

correct_answer_points: Type 1 in the Chomsky hierarchy is a context-sensitive grammar.
Context-sensitive languages are more powerful than context-free languages.
Regular grammars are Type 3 and context-free grammars are Type 2.
Recursively enumerable languages are Type 0.

options.a: Regular languages are Type 3 in the Chomsky hierarchy, not Type 1.
options.b: Context-free languages are Type 2, one level below context-sensitive languages.
options.d: Recursively enumerable languages are Type 0, the most general class in the Chomsky hierarchy.

questions.question: In XML, which attribute is used to uniquely identify an element?

correct_answer_points: The id attribute identifies a specific XML element.
An id is intended to be unique within the relevant document.
class is normally used to group multiple elements.
name and tag are not the standard answer for unique identification here.

options.b: class is normally used to group elements or apply common styling; it is not the unique identifier here.
options.c: name can label or name an element in some contexts, but it is not the standard unique XML identifier in this question.
options.d: tag identifies the element type, such as a tag name; it does not uniquely identify one element.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the traditional goal of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in terms of human-like intelligence?
options: (c) Putting human intelligence into a computer
questions.correct_answer: Putting human intelligence into a computer

correct_answer_points: Artificial Intelligence aims to make computers perform tasks that normally require human intelligence.
These tasks include reasoning, learning, perception, language understanding and problem solving.
AI systems use algorithms and data to model or reproduce intelligent behavior.
The option about putting human-like intelligence into a computer best matches this traditional textbook description.

options.a: Playing games is one application of AI, not the definition of AI itself.
options.b: Making a machine intelligent describes the broad goal of AI, but it is less specific than the traditional definition represented by option (c).
options.d: AI is a well-defined field concerned with intelligent behavior, so “none” is incorrect.

questions.question: Delphi and COCOMO are techniques used to estimate:

correct_answer_points: COCOMO estimates software development effort/cost using project characteristics.
Delphi is an expert-judgment estimation technique.
Both are commonly used for project cost/effort estimation rather than reliability measurement.
Therefore software development cost is the best option.

options.a: Software size can be estimated using measures such as LOC or function points, not specifically these two techniques.
options.b: Software reliability concerns failure behavior and dependability; Delphi and COCOMO are cost-estimation approaches.
options.c: Software complexity measures code/design complexity; it is not the main purpose of Delphi or COCOMO.

questions.question: EBCDIC is mainly used in which type of computer system?

correct_answer_points: EBCDIC is an 8-bit character encoding historically associated with IBM systems.
It is strongly associated with IBM mainframe computers.
Modern PCs mainly use ASCII/Unicode-derived encodings.
So mainframe computers is the intended answer.

options.b: Personal computers traditionally use character encodings such as ASCII/Unicode rather than EBCDIC as their main legacy encoding.
options.c: Supercomputers are not specifically identified with EBCDIC; EBCDIC is strongly associated with IBM mainframes.
options.d: Mobile devices use modern Unicode-based encodings, not EBCDIC as their primary character encoding.

questions.question: Convert the Boolean function F(A,B,C)=Σ(0,1,3,5) to its simplified SOP form.

correct_answer_points: The function contains minterms 0, 1, 3 and 5.
Grouping these minterms on a 3-variable Karnaugh map gives a′b′, a′c and b′c.
So the simplified Sum of Products (SOP) is a′b′ + a′c + b′c.
This expression covers exactly the required minterms without adding unwanted minterms.

options.a: The listed expression does not represent the required minterms correctly; it is too broad.
options.b: ab + ac covers combinations requiring A=1, so it misses required minterms where A=0.
options.c: a+b+c′ is true for many more input combinations than the four required minterms, so it is not the simplified SOP.
options.d: a′b′c represents only one minterm, so it cannot cover all four required minterms 0, 1, 3 and 5.

questions.question: Choose the correct option to fill in the blank: ____ is an online platform or website where individuals or businesses regularly publish articles/journals, called posts, on various topics.

correct_answer_points: A blog is a website or platform where posts/articles are published regularly.
Blog posts can cover news, opinions, tutorials or many other topics.
A browser is software used to access websites, not the publishing platform itself.
A web server hosts content, but the description specifically defines a blog.

options.a: A browser is software used to access web content; it is not the publishing platform described.
options.c: A newsgroup is a discussion forum for messages, not specifically a site for regularly publishing authored posts.
options.d: A web server hosts and delivers web resources; it is not the name for the publishing platform itself.

questions.question: Suppose the word is "automata". The total number of states required to recognize the word using a DFA will be ____.
options: (d) The word cannot be recognized using DFA

correct_answer_points: The word “automata” has 8 characters.
A DFA recognizing exactly one fixed word normally needs one state for each prefix plus an accepting state transition structure.
Thus 8 characters require 9 states including the final accepting state.
This is the standard fixed-string DFA construction.

options.b: A DFA that recognizes exactly one fixed word of length 8 needs a state for each matched prefix plus a final state, giving 9 states.
options.c: 10 states are unnecessary for the standard minimal DFA for one fixed word of length 8.
options.d: Every finite language, including a single word such as “automata”, can be recognized by a DFA.

questions.question: Stack works on the principle of:

correct_answer_points: A stack follows LIFO: Last In, First Out.
The most recently pushed item is the first item popped.
This differs from a queue, which follows FIFO.
Function-call stacks are a common real-world example.

options.a: A stack does not select the middle item first; insertion/removal happens at one end.
options.b: FIFO is the rule for a queue, where the oldest item leaves first.
options.d: “Last In Last Out” is not the standard name for stack behavior; the standard term is LIFO.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a property of knowledge representation?

correct_answer_points: Standard knowledge-representation properties include representational adequacy.
They also include inferential adequacy and inferential efficiency.
Acquisitional efficiency is another commonly cited property.
“Representational verification” is not the standard property listed in the options.

options.b: Representational adequacy is a standard knowledge-representation property, so it cannot be the answer.
options.c: Inferential adequacy is a standard property describing the ability to derive new facts from represented knowledge.
options.d: Inferential efficiency is also a standard concern in knowledge representation.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of the backtracking approach in solving the Hamiltonian cycle problem?
options: (a) To find a cycle with the fewest edges
(b) To find a cycle with the lowest weight
(c) To find a cycle that visits every vertex exactly once
(d) To find a cycle with the maximum number of edges
questions.correct_answer: To find a cycle that visits every vertex exactly once

correct_answer_points: A Hamiltonian cycle must visit every vertex exactly once and return to the start.
Backtracking builds a candidate path step by step.
When a partial path cannot lead to a valid Hamiltonian cycle, it backtracks.
Therefore the target is a cycle visiting every vertex exactly once.

options.a: A Hamiltonian cycle is not defined by having the fewest edges; it must include every vertex once.
options.b: Lowest weight is relevant to weighted optimization problems, not the basic Hamiltonian-cycle definition.
options.d: The goal is not to maximize edges; a Hamiltonian cycle has a fixed number of edges equal to the number of vertices.

questions.question: Software developed only to detect and remove viruses is called ____.

correct_answer_points: Antivirus software is specifically designed to detect, block and remove malware/viruses.
Malware is the harmful software category itself, not the removal tool.
Spyware is a type of malicious software that monitors users.
Adware primarily displays unwanted advertising.

options.a: Malware is the broad category of malicious software, including viruses; it is not the specific protective program.
options.c: Spyware secretly collects information from a system; it is malware, not software designed to remove viruses.
options.d: Adware displays unwanted advertisements and may track behavior; it is not an antivirus utility.

questions.question: Assertion (A): CSS is an attribute of the table tag and is used to style Tables on a web page. Reason (R): CSS is used to apply styles like font, color, and spacing in an HTML document.
options: (a) Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation
(b) Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation
(c) A is correct but R is false
(d) A is false but R is true
questions.correct_answer: A is false but R is true

correct_answer_points: CSS is not an attribute of the table tag; it is a styling language used with HTML.
CSS can style tables using selectors and properties.
Therefore the Assertion is false.
The Reason is true, so the correct assertion-reason choice is D.

options.a: The Assertion is false because CSS is not an attribute of the table tag; it is a styling language. Therefore this “both true” choice is wrong.
options.b: The Assertion is false, so a choice saying both statements are correct cannot be right.
options.c: The Reason is true, so this option incorrectly claims the Reason is false.

questions.question: The greedy search strategy chooses a node for expansion in ____.

correct_answer_points: Greedy best-first search selects the node with the best heuristic value.
A common heuristic is an estimate of remaining cost to the goal.
It does not necessarily choose the shallowest or deepest node.
Hence minimum heuristic cost is the intended answer.

options.a: Shallowest-node expansion describes breadth-first search, not greedy best-first search.
options.b: Deepest-node expansion describes depth-first search.
options.c: Greedy search uses a heuristic estimate; “closest to the goal” is an informal idea, but the formal selection rule here is minimum heuristic value.

questions.question: The main advantage of the overlay technique in memory management is that it allows:
options: (a) Processes to be loaded into memory as memory
(c) Large programs to be executed on a system with limited memory
(d) Processes to communicate directly with each other
questions.correct_answer: Large programs to be executed on a system with limited memory

correct_answer_points: Overlaying lets only the needed parts of a large program reside in memory at a time.
This was historically useful when physical memory was smaller than the program.
Different program modules can reuse the same memory region.
Thus it allows large programs to run with limited memory.

options.a: Overlay does not simply load processes “as memory”; it loads only needed program portions into available memory.
options.b: Sharing memory is a separate memory-management/interprocess concern, not the main purpose of overlays.
options.d: Direct process communication is IPC and is unrelated to the primary benefit of overlays.

questions.question: Full form of MQTT is ____.

correct_answer_points: MQTT expands to Message Queuing Telemetry Transport.
It is a lightweight messaging protocol widely used in IoT.
It normally follows a publish/subscribe communication model.
The other expansions in the options are incorrect.

options.a: This is not the standard expansion of MQTT; the phrase “Multi-Queue” is incorrect.
options.b: “Multiple Queueing” is not part of the official expansion of MQTT.
options.c: The official expansion is Message Queuing Telemetry Transport; “Things” is incorrect here.

questions.question: The easiest way we can transfer control is when the old backup site sends ____ to the old primary.

correct_answer_points: A redo log records changes needed to reproduce committed updates.
Redo information is important during database recovery and failover.
An undo log serves a different rollback-oriented purpose.
Therefore redo log is the intended answer.

options.b: “Primary log” is not the standard log type named for replaying committed changes during recovery.
options.c: Undo logs support rollback/undo operations; redo logs are used to reproduce updates.
options.d: The question asks for the specific log used to transfer/replay changes, so “all” is not appropriate.

questions.question: To convert a gray code to its binary equivalent, which technique is generally used?

correct_answer_points: Gray-to-binary conversion uses cumulative XOR operations.
The binary MSB equals the Gray MSB.
Each next binary bit is obtained by XORing the previous binary bit with the current Gray bit.
So XOR is the key operation.

options.a: Subtraction is not the standard operation for Gray-to-binary conversion.
options.b: Ordinary addition is not the rule used to derive successive binary bits from Gray code.
options.d: Division has no role in the standard Gray-to-binary conversion process.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a Domain Name System server in networking?
options: (b) To convert domain names into IP addresses
(d) To establish secure connections between devices
questions.correct_answer: To convert domain names into IP addresses

correct_answer_points: DNS stands for Domain Name System.
It translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.
This lets users use names such as example.com instead of numeric addresses.
DNS is not primarily an encryption or traffic-regulation protocol.

options.a: Encryption protects confidentiality; DNS primarily performs name resolution.
options.c: Traffic regulation is handled by routing, congestion-control, firewalls, QoS and related mechanisms, not DNS itself.
options.d: Secure connections are established with mechanisms such as TLS; DNS alone does not create them.

questions.question: A popular method of organizing a wireless network topology is?

correct_answer_points: The source lists “Cluster” as the wireless topology choice.
Clustered organization groups related nodes around a coordinator or cluster structure.
The other options are not topology names in this context.
So the intended source answer is Cluster.

options.a: Software is not a wireless network topology.
options.b: “Network” is a general term, not the specific topology choice intended by the source.
options.c: Synchronization is a coordination concept, not a wireless topology name.

questions.question: Which is not an encryption technique?

correct_answer_points: AES, DES and RSA are cryptographic algorithms.
FTP is a file-transfer protocol.
FTP by itself does not provide encryption for transferred data.
Therefore FTP is not an encryption technique.

options.a: AES is a symmetric encryption standard used to protect data.
options.b: DES is an older symmetric encryption algorithm.
options.c: RSA is an asymmetric cryptographic algorithm; it is also an encryption technique.

questions.question: In BFS, vertices are explored level by level, starting from:

correct_answer_points: BFS means Breadth-First Search.
It explores all vertices at the current distance before moving farther away.
Therefore it begins at the shallowest level and progresses outward.
A queue is typically used to implement this traversal.

options.a: Starting at the deepest level describes depth-first behavior, not BFS.
options.c: BFS does not begin at a special middle level; it begins at the source and expands outward by levels.
options.d: Highest degree is not the rule used by BFS; BFS follows queue-based level-order exploration.

questions.question: Consider the following Python dictionary: D={'SO1':95, 'SO2':96}. For l in D: print(l, end='#'). What is the output?

correct_answer_points: Iterating directly over a Python dictionary yields its keys by default.
The keys here are SO1 and SO2.
The end parameter adds # after each printed key.
Therefore the output is SO1#SO2#.

options.b: Iterating over a dictionary yields keys, not values, so 95#96# is not produced.
options.c: The loop variable receives only each key, so Python does not print key-value pairs here.

questions.question: Why do we need Industry 4.0?

correct_answer_points: Industry 4.0 promotes connected, automated and data-driven industry.
It can help predict or detect machine failures.
Automation and monitoring can improve operational safety.
Therefore the “all of the above” option is the intended answer.

options.a: Detecting machine failures is one Industry 4.0 use, but it is not the only reason for adopting it.
options.b: Preventive maintenance is an important benefit, but Industry 4.0 also targets safety, productivity and connected automation.
options.c: Improving safety is a benefit, but the question asks for the combined set of listed benefits.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following statement: print(14%3**2*4)?

correct_answer_points: Exponentiation has higher precedence than modulo and multiplication.
3**2 evaluates to 9.
14%9 gives 5, and 5*4 gives 20.
So the output is 20.

options.a: 16 would result from a different evaluation; Python first evaluates 3**2, then modulo, then multiplication.
options.b: 64 does not follow Python operator precedence for the expression.
options.d: 256 is inconsistent with the actual intermediate result 14%9 = 5.

questions.question: Which function should be used to retrieve the first few rows of a DataFrame?

correct_answer_points: pandas DataFrame.head(n) returns the first n rows.
It is commonly used for a quick inspection of tabular data.
print(n), get(n) and call(n) are not the standard DataFrame method for this task.
Therefore head(n) is correct.

options.a: print(n) prints a value; it is not the pandas DataFrame method for selecting the first rows.
options.c: get(n) is not the standard DataFrame method for returning the first n rows.
options.d: call(n) is not the pandas DataFrame method used for this purpose.

questions.question: Which form of e-marketplace brings together buyers and sellers from multiple industries, often for MRO materials?

correct_answer_points: A horizontal e-marketplace serves buyers and sellers across multiple industries.
MRO materials can be purchased by organizations from many industries.
A vertical marketplace focuses on one industry or sector.
Therefore Horizontal is the intended choice.

options.b: A vertical marketplace focuses on a particular industry or sector rather than multiple industries.
options.c: Integrated is not the standard marketplace classification intended here.
options.d: A standalone marketplace is not the multi-industry MRO marketplace described.

questions.question: Which software life cycle model is based on iterative prototyping?

correct_answer_points: The Spiral model develops software through repeated cycles.
Each cycle can include prototyping, risk analysis and refinement.
Waterfall is primarily sequential.
Hence Spiral is the expected answer for iterative prototyping.

options.a: Waterfall is mainly sequential, with limited iteration between phases.
options.c: Agile is iterative and incremental, but the specific model traditionally based around iterative prototyping and risk analysis is Spiral.
options.d: The Prototype model emphasizes building prototypes, but the source’s intended model is Spiral because it combines iteration with risk analysis.

questions.question: The dining philosophers problem is an example of a synchronization problem in:

correct_answer_points: The dining philosophers problem is a classic synchronization/concurrency problem.
Philosophers compete for shared resources such as forks.
The problem illustrates deadlock and mutual-exclusion issues.
Thus mutual exclusion is the relevant concept.

options.a: Process scheduling decides which process gets CPU time; it is not the central issue demonstrated by dining philosophers.
options.c: Memory allocation deals with assigning memory space, not competing access to shared forks/resources.
options.d: Interrupt handling is unrelated to the classic synchronization problem.

questions.question: Which of the following conversions is not possible algorithmically?
options: (a) From regular grammar to context-free grammar
(b) From nondeterministic pushdown automata to deterministic pushdown automata
(c) From nondeterministic finite-state automata to deterministic finite-state automata
(d) From nondeterministic Turing machine to deterministic Turing machine
questions.correct_answer: From nondeterministic pushdown automata to deterministic pushdown automata

correct_answer_points: Nondeterministic finite automata can be converted to deterministic finite automata.
Nondeterministic Turing machines have equivalent deterministic Turing machines.
Regular grammars can be related to context-free grammars.
General nondeterministic pushdown automata cannot be converted to equivalent deterministic PDAs in all cases.

options.a: Regular grammars can be represented as context-free grammars, so this conversion is possible.
options.c: An NFA can be converted to an equivalent DFA using subset construction.
options.d: Nondeterministic and deterministic Turing machines have the same computational power and can simulate each other.
options.b: A general nondeterministic pushdown automaton cannot always be converted into an equivalent deterministic pushdown automaton because deterministic PDAs recognize a proper subset of context-free languages.

questions.question: De Morgan’s theorems are particularly useful in simplifying logic expressions that contain a large number of ___.

correct_answer_points: De Morgan’s theorems transform AND/OR combinations using complements.
They are especially useful when Boolean expressions contain many operators.
For example, NOT(A AND B) becomes NOT A OR NOT B.
Thus operators is the intended answer.

options.a: De Morgan’s laws transform complements of AND/OR combinations; they are not primarily about reducing the number of variables.
options.b: Constants may occur in logic expressions, but De Morgan’s laws specifically target logical operators and complemented expressions.
options.c: Terms are affected during simplification, but the key transformation is between AND/OR operators under complementation.

questions.question: Which of the following devices is required to set up a wired LAN?

correct_answer_points: A NIC (Network Interface Card) provides a network interface for a computer.
It connects the device to the LAN medium.
A modem is for specific WAN/ISP connections, not required for every wired LAN.
A repeater and firewall serve different networking roles.

options.a: A modem converts between network signaling technologies and is not required for every wired LAN.
options.c: A repeater extends a signal; it can be useful but is not the basic interface every wired LAN device needs.
options.d: A firewall provides security filtering; it is not the required network interface for a wired LAN connection.

questions.question: Which of the following is an extension of the basic model of a Turing machine?

correct_answer_points: Multi-tape, multi-head and nondeterministic Turing machines are standard extensions/variants.
They increase convenience or change the machine model without changing Turing computability in the usual sense.
Each can be studied as an extension of the basic single-tape deterministic model.
Therefore all of the above is correct.

options.a: A multi-tape Turing machine is a standard extension of the basic model.
options.b: A multi-head Turing machine is also an extension of the basic single-tape/single-head model.
options.c: A nondeterministic Turing machine is another formal extension with equivalent computational power.

questions.question: For a DFA that accepts binary numbers whose decimal equivalent is divisible by 3, what are all the possible remainders?

correct_answer_points: A number divisible by 3 has remainder 0 when divided by 3.
Any integer division by 3 can only produce remainders 0, 1 or 2.
Remainder 3 is impossible.
So the possible remainders are 0, 1 and 2.

options.a: Remainder 0 is possible, but it is not the only possible remainder for arbitrary binary inputs.
options.b: Remainder 1 is also possible, so the pair 0,2 is incomplete.
options.d: Remainder 3 cannot occur when dividing by 3 because remainders must be less than the divisor.

questions.question: What is the full form of WSN?

correct_answer_points: WSN stands for Wireless Sensor Network.
A WSN contains distributed sensor nodes that collect measurements from their surroundings.
The nodes communicate wirelessly and can forward collected data to a central system or other nodes.
WSNs are commonly used in IoT, environmental monitoring, industrial monitoring and smart systems.

options.a: Wireless Standard Protocol is not the expansion of WSN; the abbreviation refers to a network of wireless sensors.
options.b: Wireless Sensor Protocol is not the standard expansion; WSN refers to Wireless Sensor Network.
options.c: Wireless Serial Protocol is unrelated to the standard meaning of WSN.
options.d: Wireless Single Protocol is not the standard expansion of WSN.

questions.question: Which keyword in C# is used to prevent a class from being inherited by other classes?

correct_answer_points: In C#, the sealed keyword prevents a class from being inherited.
A sealed class can still be instantiated and used normally unless other restrictions apply.
The keyword controls inheritance; it does not mean the class or its objects cannot be used.
In Java, the equivalent keyword for preventing inheritance is final.

options.b: In Java, final prevents a class from being inherited, but C# uses sealed for this purpose.
options.c: private controls member/class accessibility; it is not the keyword used specifically to prevent inheritance.
options.d: static makes a member belong to the class rather than instances; it does not prevent inheritance.

questions.question: What is the full name of SCADA?

correct_answer_points: SCADA stands for Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition.
It is used to monitor and control industrial processes.
SCADA systems collect data from field devices and present it to operators.
The other expansions are incorrect.

options.a: SCADA stands for Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition; “Document” is incorrect.
options.c: “Column” and “Assessment” are not part of the standard expansion.
options.d: The final word should be Acquisition, not Assessment.

questions.question: The cost estimation technique that involves expert judgment and consensus is called:

correct_answer_points: The Delphi method gathers expert opinions, often anonymously, over multiple rounds.
It seeks convergence or consensus among experts.
COCOMO is a parametric software cost model.
Therefore Delphi method is correct.

options.a: COCOMO estimates effort/cost using an algorithmic model rather than relying mainly on group expert consensus.
options.c: Waterfall is a software life-cycle model, not an estimation technique.
options.d: Prototype model is a development approach, not an expert-consensus cost-estimation method.

questions.question: When using the parity bit method, how does the receiver determine if an error occurred during transmission?
options: (a) By counting the number of ones in the data
(b) By comparing the parity bit with the data
(d) By comparing the number of ones with the parity bit
questions.correct_answer: By comparing the number of ones with the parity bit

correct_answer_points: Parity checking counts the number of 1 bits according to the selected parity rule.
The receiver examines the received data together with the parity bit.
A mismatch indicates that the expected parity condition is not satisfied.
Thus comparing the observed number of ones with the parity bit captures the intended check.

options.a: Simply counting ones without considering the expected parity rule is incomplete; the receiver must check the parity condition including the parity bit.
options.b: The receiver does not compare the parity bit as an isolated value; it checks parity across the received bits.
options.c: Modulo arithmetic can describe parity mathematically, but it is not the direct procedure stated in the options.

questions.question: Evaluate the given postfix expression: 3 5 * 6 + 2 3 * -

correct_answer_points: Postfix expressions are evaluated with a stack.
3 5 * gives 15; then +6 gives 21.
2 3 * gives 6; finally 21-6 gives 15.
Therefore the result is 15.

options.a: The stack calculation gives 15, not 39.
options.c: 21 is an intermediate value after 3*5+6, before subtracting 2*3.
options.d: 12 does not follow the postfix stack operations.

questions.question: Which of the following is a mapped data type?

correct_answer_points: A Python dictionary maps keys to values.
It is therefore a mapped/associative data type.
Lists and sets are collection types but do not provide the same key-to-value mapping.
Hence Dictionary is correct.

options.a: A list is a sequence type, not a mapping of keys to values.
options.b: A set stores unique elements and is not a key-value mapping.
options.d: Boolean stores True/False values; it is not a mapping type.

questions.question: Each ___ represents a specific color.

correct_answer_points: In raster images, each pixel stores color information.
A pixel value encodes the intensity/color components for that location.
A frame or character is not the basic color unit of an image.
Therefore Pixel value is correct.

options.a: A frame is a complete image or video unit; it contains many pixels rather than representing one specific color.
options.b: A character represents text data, not a color value.
options.d: A specific color in a digital image is represented by pixel values, so “none” is incorrect.

questions.question: In general, a file is basically a collection of all related ___.

correct_answer_points: A file is a collection of related records.
A record contains related fields describing one entity/item.
Fields are smaller components inside records.
Therefore records is the intended answer.

options.a: Rows and columns describe tabular organization, but the traditional definition of a file is a collection of related records.
options.b: A database contains organized collections of data/files; it is not simply a collection of related fields.
options.c: Fields are individual data attributes within records, not the complete units collected in a file.

questions.question: A universal Turing machine is a:

correct_answer_points: A universal Turing machine can simulate other Turing machines based on their descriptions.
It is therefore programmable/reprogrammable rather than tied to one fixed computation.
“Universal” refers to its ability to emulate arbitrary machines of the model.
Hence reprogrammable Turing machine is correct.

options.a: A universal Turing machine is not limited to one tape; universality concerns simulation of other machines.
options.b: It is not defined specifically as a two-tape machine.
options.d: The universal machine is not “all of the above” because universality does not require a particular tape count.

questions.question: Which statement is used to retrieve data from a database in SQL?

correct_answer_points: SELECT is the SQL statement used to retrieve data.
UPDATE changes existing rows.
DELETE removes rows and INSERT adds rows.
Therefore SELECT is correct.

options.b: UPDATE changes existing rows; it does not retrieve result sets.
options.c: DELETE removes rows from a table.
options.d: INSERT adds new rows to a table.

questions.question: In HTML, we start a comment using:

correct_answer_points: HTML comments begin with <!-- and end with -->.
Comment text is ignored by the browser’s rendering engine.
The other symbols are not the standard opening delimiter.
Therefore <!-- is correct.

options.a: <I is not the HTML comment opening delimiter.
options.b: -> is not used to begin an HTML comment.
options.c: => is not an HTML comment delimiter.

questions.question: How are cookies typically stored on a client’s device?

correct_answer_points: Traditional web cookies are commonly stored as small name-value data in the browser/client.
They can persist for a session or for a specified expiration time.
They are not normally stored as a database on the client.
Among the supplied choices, plain text file is the intended answer.

options.b: A client browser does not normally store each cookie as a conventional database exposed to the user.
options.c: Cookies are not required to be encrypted; sensitive protection depends on mechanisms such as Secure/HttpOnly and HTTPS.
options.d: The browser manages cookies separately; browser cache is a different storage concept.

questions.question: There are ___ layers in the Zigbee architecture.

correct_answer_points: The classic Zigbee protocol stack is commonly described using four layers: PHY, MAC, Network and Application.
IEEE 802.15.4 supplies the PHY and MAC foundations.
Zigbee adds network and application-related layers above them.
Therefore the intended answer is 4.

options.b: The classic Zigbee stack is commonly described as four layers, so five is not the intended answer here.
options.c: Six is not the standard four-layer Zigbee architecture used by this question.
options.d: Seven is also not the intended layer count.

questions.question: Assertion (A): It becomes difficult to update and maintain the design of a website using CSS. Reason (R): CSS allows web developers to separate the presentation layer (styles and layout) from the content layer (HTML).
options: (a) Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation
(b) Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation
(c) A is correct but R is false
(d) A is false but R is true
questions.correct_answer: A is false but R is true

correct_answer_points: The Assertion is false because CSS generally makes website design easier to maintain, not harder.
CSS separates presentation such as colors, fonts and layout from HTML content.
Changing a shared CSS rule can update the appearance of many elements at once.
Therefore the Assertion is false while the Reason is true.

options.a: This choice requires both statements to be true, but the Assertion incorrectly says CSS makes maintenance difficult.
options.b: The Assertion is false, so a choice that treats both statements as true cannot apply.
options.c: The Reason is true because CSS separates presentation from HTML content, so this choice incorrectly marks the Reason as false.

questions.question: In the backtracking approach to the 8-Queens problem, once a possible solution is found, the algorithm:
options: (b) Continues to search for more solutions
(d) Rearranges the queens to optimize the solution
questions.correct_answer: Continues to search for more solutions

correct_answer_points: Backtracking does not have to stop after the first solution when the task is to find solutions generally.
After a solution, it can backtrack and continue searching for additional valid placements.
The search prunes invalid partial solutions.
Thus “continues to search for more solutions” is the intended answer.

options.a: If the task is to find all solutions, finding one valid arrangement does not necessarily stop the search.
options.c: The algorithm does not blindly enumerate every possibility; backtracking prunes invalid partial solutions.
options.d: 8-Queens is a constraint-satisfaction problem; it does not optimize a numerical queen arrangement.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used to extract or filter data and information from a data warehouse?

correct_answer_points: Data retrieval tools help query and extract warehouse information.
Data mining discovers patterns and useful knowledge from stored data.
Both are valid ways of extracting/filtering or deriving information.
Therefore Both B and C is the intended option.

options.a: Data redundancy means duplicated data; it is a data-quality/storage issue, not a retrieval tool.
options.b: Data-retrieval tools can extract/filter warehouse information, so this option alone is incomplete when data mining is also considered.
options.c: Data mining can discover useful patterns and information, but the source intends both retrieval tools and mining.

questions.question: Which algorithm can be optimized to meet the deadline and rate requirements of continuous media?

correct_answer_points: EDF schedules work according to the nearest deadline.
SCAN-EDF combines deadline considerations with disk/continuous-media scheduling ideas.
Both can be used for deadline/rate-sensitive continuous media scheduling.
Hence the source answer is Both EDF and SCAN-EDF.

options.a: EDF is a deadline-based scheduler and can support real-time media requirements, but the source asks for the combined option including SCAN-EDF.
options.b: SCAN-EDF is useful for continuous-media/disk scheduling, but the source treats both algorithms as applicable.
options.d: Both EDF and SCAN-EDF are relevant in the source context, so “none” is incorrect.

questions.question: The quality of __ remains unchanged even when its size is increased or decreased.

correct_answer_points: Vector graphics are defined mathematically using paths/shapes rather than fixed pixels.
Scaling them up or down does not inherently reduce geometric resolution.
Raster photos become pixelated when enlarged sufficiently.
Therefore vector graphics is correct.

options.b: Ordinary raster-like drawings can lose quality when enlarged; vector graphics retain mathematical shapes.
options.c: Photos are raster images, so enlarging them can reveal pixels and reduce apparent quality.
options.d: Line art can be raster or vector; the defining scalable property in the question is vector representation.

questions.question: How many inputs are there in a full-adder circuit for each individual binary digit being added or subtracted?

correct_answer_points: A full adder adds three one-bit inputs.
The inputs are A, B and carry-in (Cin).
It produces sum and carry-out outputs.
Therefore it has 3 inputs.

options.a: A full adder adds two operand bits plus an incoming carry, so one input is insufficient.
options.b: Two inputs are enough for a half adder, but not a full adder because a carry-in is also required.
options.d: A standard full adder has three inputs, not four.

questions.question: What does ‘https’ stand for in a Web Address?
options: (a) The website is hosted on a local server
(b) The website is a search engine
(c) The website uses standard HTTP protocol
(d) The website is secured using encryption
questions.correct_answer: The website is secured using encryption

correct_answer_points: HTTPS means HTTP Secure in common usage.
It uses TLS to protect HTTP communication.
Encryption helps prevent third parties from reading or modifying protected traffic.
Thus the intended option is that the website is secured using encryption.

options.a: HTTPS is independent of whether the website is hosted locally or remotely.
options.b: HTTPS can be used by search engines, stores, blogs and many other websites; it is not a search-engine indicator.
options.c: HTTPS is HTTP carried over TLS/SSL, providing security; it is more than simply standard HTTP.

questions.question: What is an entity in DTD?

correct_answer_points: A DTD entity can refer to replacement text or an external entity resource.
An external entity specifically references an external resource.
It is not a mathematical equation or JavaScript function.
Therefore the supplied “reference to an external resource” option is the intended answer.

options.b: An XML DTD entity is not a mathematical equation.
options.c: An entity is not a special XML element/tag; it is a named replacement or reference mechanism.
options.d: DTD entities are part of XML/DTD syntax, not JavaScript functions.

questions.question: Which technique provides the highest level of customization for implementing digital logic circuits?

correct_answer_points: FPGA devices are highly programmable and can implement customized digital logic.
They can be reconfigured after manufacturing.
ROM and PLA designs are programmable but generally offer less flexibility for complex custom logic.
Therefore FPGA-based design provides the highest customization among these choices.

options.a: ROM-based logic uses stored truth tables but offers less general reconfigurability than an FPGA.
options.b: PLA-based logic is programmable, but an FPGA provides much greater configurable logic resources.
options.d: Gate arrays provide customization at the hardware level, but an FPGA generally offers higher post-manufacturing flexibility.

questions.question: Auxiliary storage space management in an operating system includes:
options: (b) Managing input/output operations between processes and devices
(d) Managing the allocation of space on secondary storage devices
questions.correct_answer: Managing the allocation of space on secondary storage devices

correct_answer_points: Auxiliary storage means secondary storage such as disks/SSDs.
Its management includes allocating and tracking storage space.
CPU registers and process memory allocation are separate concerns.
Therefore secondary-storage space allocation is correct.

options.a: CPU registers are managed by the processor architecture, not by auxiliary-storage management.
options.b: This describes I/O management rather than the allocation of disk/secondary-storage space.
options.c: Process memory allocation belongs to main-memory management, not auxiliary storage management.

questions.question: Which programming paradigm focuses on breaking a program down into smaller procedures or functions?

correct_answer_points: Procedural programming organizes programs around procedures/functions.
Large tasks are decomposed into smaller routines that operate on data.
Object-oriented programming instead centers on objects/classes.
Therefore procedural programming is correct.

options.a: OOP organizes programs around objects/classes and their interactions.
options.c: Functional programming emphasizes functions and expressions, often avoiding mutable state.
options.d: Imperative programming is broader and focuses on commands/state changes; the specific procedure-oriented paradigm is procedural programming.

questions.question: Which of the following is a DML command in SQL?

correct_answer_points: UPDATE is a DML command because it changes rows in existing tables.
CREATE, ALTER and DROP are DDL commands.
DML operates on table data; DDL defines or changes database structure.
Therefore UPDATE is correct.

options.b: CREATE is a DDL command used to define database objects.
options.c: ALTER is DDL used to modify the structure of a database object.
options.d: DROP is DDL used to remove a database object.

questions.question: Which memory management technique uses fixed-size blocks of memory, allowing processes to be loaded into any available block?

correct_answer_points: Paging divides logical memory into fixed-size pages and physical memory into fixed-size frames.
A page can be placed in any available compatible frame.
Segmentation uses variable-size logical segments.
Therefore Paging is correct.

options.b: Segmentation uses variable-size logical segments, not fixed-size blocks.
options.c: Virtual memory is a broader memory-management technique; it may use paging but is not itself the fixed-block technique.
options.d: Relocation adjusts addresses when loading/moving a process; it is not the fixed-size block allocation method.

questions.question: What is the value of the following expression? 3+3.00, 3**3.0

correct_answer_points: The comma creates a tuple containing two expression results.
3+3.00 evaluates to 6.0 because 3.00 is a float.
3**3.0 evaluates to 27.0.
Therefore Python displays (6.0, 27.0).

options.a: The two expressions form a tuple, and their values are 6.0 and 27.0, so the listed bracket form is incorrect.
options.c: The first result is 6.0 because 3.00 is a float, and the exponent result is also 27.0.

questions.question: Musa’s basic model is used to measure:

correct_answer_points: Musa’s basic model is associated with software reliability measurement.
It models failure occurrence over execution/testing time.
The model is used to estimate reliability-related measures rather than software size.
Note: the supplied source labels “software size” as the option; that conflicts with the standard Musa model description.

options.a: Musa’s model is a software reliability growth model, not a complexity model.
options.b: This expression is not one of the valid simplified forms for the given function.
options.c: Software performance concerns speed/resource behavior; Musa’s basic model estimates reliability/failure behavior.

questions.question: Applications of AI include ____.

correct_answer_points: AI includes game-playing and other intelligent applications.
Expert systems are classic AI applications.
Machine learning and deep learning are major modern AI approaches.
Therefore all of the above is correct.

options.a: Gaming is an AI application, but it is only one example.
options.b: Expert systems are AI applications, but they are not the complete set listed in the question.
options.c: Machine learning and deep learning are major AI approaches/applications, but the question includes gaming and expert systems too.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Software Requirements Specification (SRS) documents?
options: (a) To list the programming languages to be used
(b) To describe the user interface design
(c) To define the functional and non-functional requirements of the software
(d) To specify the required hardware components
questions.correct_answer: To define the functional and non-functional requirements of the software

correct_answer_points: An SRS documents what the software must do.
It captures functional and non-functional requirements.
Programming languages, UI design and hardware choices may be specified elsewhere or later.
Therefore defining functional and non-functional requirements is correct.

options.a: SRS may mention constraints, but its primary purpose is not to choose programming languages.
options.b: UI design can be specified separately; SRS primarily defines what the system must do and its constraints/quality requirements.
options.d: Hardware requirements may appear as constraints, but they are not the main purpose of the SRS.

questions.question: Assertion (A): In Python, every object is assigned a unique identity (ID). Reason (R): The ID remains the same for the lifetime of that object.
options: (a) Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation
(b) Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation
(c) A is correct but R is false
(d) A is false but R is true
questions.correct_answer: Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation

correct_answer_points: Every Python object has an identity that can be obtained using the built-in id() function.
An object's identity remains associated with that object for its lifetime.
Both the Assertion and the Reason are therefore true.
The lifetime property describes how the identity behaves, but it does not explain why Python assigns an identity to every object.

options.a: The Reason is true, but it does not explain why every object is assigned an identity, so the explanation relationship is incorrect.
options.c: The Reason is true because an object's identity remains stable during its lifetime.
options.d: The Assertion is true because Python objects have identities, so this choice incorrectly marks it as false.

questions.question: Software engineering emerged due to:

correct_answer_points: Software engineering developed as software systems became larger and harder to build reliably.
Projects faced cost, schedule, quality and maintenance problems.
These challenges motivated systematic engineering processes.
Therefore challenges posed by software development is correct.

options.a: Software engineering did not emerge because computer technology declined; computing was expanding rapidly.
options.b: The key problem was managing complex software development, not primarily complex hardware.
options.d: Software engineering exists precisely because software became a major engineering concern, not because of hardware-only solutions.

questions.question: The minimum number of productions required to generate a language consisting of palindrome strings over Σ={a,b} is:

correct_answer_points: A compact grammar can generate palindromes using two recursive rules plus base cases.
For example, S→aSa, S→bSb, S→a, S→b, and optionally ε for even-length palindromes.
This gives five productions when ε is included as a base case formulation.
Therefore 5 is the intended answer for the source question.

options.a: Three productions are not enough for the usual grammar construction that covers the required palindrome cases.
options.b: Seven productions are more than the intended minimum for the standard compact construction.
options.d: Six productions are not the minimum in the source formulation; five is the intended answer.

questions.question: A socket is used for:

correct_answer_points: A socket is an endpoint for communication between processes.
It can connect processes on the same or different machines through networking.
Sockets are widely used by TCP/UDP applications.
Therefore process-to-process communication is correct.

options.a: A socket is a software communication endpoint, not a physical transmission medium/device.
options.c: Data compression changes representation size; a socket provides a communication endpoint.
options.d: Network management is broader than the endpoint-to-endpoint communication provided by a socket.

questions.question: SFTP is used for:
options: (a) Sending files securely over the Internet
(b) Sending mail securely over the Internet
questions.correct_answer: Sending files securely over the Internet

correct_answer_points: SFTP is SSH File Transfer Protocol.
It transfers files over an encrypted SSH connection.
It is designed for secure file transfer, not email or video conferencing.
Therefore sending files securely over the Internet is correct.

options.b: SFTP transfers files securely; it is not primarily a secure email protocol.
options.c: Video conferencing uses real-time media protocols, not SFTP.
options.d: Secure chat uses messaging protocols; SFTP is specifically for file transfer.

questions.question: In Karnaugh Maps, which term refers to a group of adjacent cells that can be combined to simplify a logic expression?

correct_answer_points: A Karnaugh map simplifies Boolean expressions by grouping adjacent cells.
A valid group contains a power-of-two number of adjacent cells.
Such groups produce simplified implicants.
The source uses “Group” as the intended term.

options.a: “Block” is a general term, but the standard K-map term for adjacent cells grouped for simplification is a group.
options.b: “Cluster” is not the standard K-map term used for a simplification grouping.
options.c: A pair is a valid group size of two cells, but it is only one possible group size, not the general term.

questions.question: Which version of IP address is most suitable for IoT?

correct_answer_points: IPv6 provides a vastly larger address space than IPv4.
IoT can involve enormous numbers of connected devices.
IPv6 also supports features useful for modern IP networks.
Therefore IPv6 is the most suitable choice.

options.a: IPv4 has a much smaller address space and is harder to scale to the huge number of IoT devices.
options.b: IPv5 was never deployed as the successor addressing protocol for the Internet.
options.d: IPv7 is not the standard deployed IP version for IoT; IPv6 provides the needed address space.

questions.question: What is the term for defining multiple methods in a class with the same name but different parameters?

correct_answer_points: Overloading means multiple methods share the same name but have different parameter lists.
The compiler/runtime selects the appropriate method based on the call signature.
Overriding instead replaces inherited behavior with a new implementation.
Therefore Overloading is correct.

options.a: Overriding means redefining an inherited method with the same signature; it is different from changing parameters in the same class.
options.c: “Inherited” describes receiving members from a parent class, not defining same-name methods with different parameters.
options.d: Inheritance is the mechanism of deriving a class from another class; it is not method overloading.

questions.question: Assertion (A): SMS is the acronym for Smart Message Service. Reason (R): SMS is the most common technique for delivering short, clear, and important messages quickly.
options: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation
(b) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation
(c) A is true but R is false
(d) A is false but R is true
questions.correct_answer: A is false but R is true

correct_answer_points: SMS stands for Short Message Service, so the Assertion's expansion 'Smart Message Service' is incorrect.
SMS is designed for sending short text messages over mobile communication networks.
Its widespread use makes it a common method for delivering short messages quickly.
Therefore the Assertion is false while the Reason is true.

options.a: The Assertion is false because SMS means Short Message Service, not Smart Message Service.
options.b: The Assertion is false, so both statements cannot be true.
options.c: The Assertion is false, so this choice incorrectly treats it as true.

questions.question: Process-to-process communication involves communication between the following:
options: (b) Different devices on the same network

correct_answer_points: Process-to-process communication occurs between communicating processes.
Those processes may reside on different devices across a network.
Network layers and protocols are mechanisms supporting the communication.
Therefore processes on different devices is the intended answer.

options.a: Different network layers communicate using defined interfaces/services; that is not what process-to-process communication means.
options.b: Different devices can communicate, but process-to-process communication specifically identifies application/process endpoints.
options.c: Protocol differences do not define process-to-process communication.

questions.question: What are the three main types of DBMS?
options: (a) Relational DBMS, Hierarchical DBMS, and Network DBMS
(b) Relational DBMS, Object Oriented DBMS, and NoSQL DBMS
(c) Hierarchical DBMS, Network DBMS, and Object Oriented DBMS
(d) NoSQL DBMS, Object Oriented DBMS, and Relational DBMS
questions.correct_answer: Relational DBMS, Hierarchical DBMS, and Network DBMS

correct_answer_points: Traditional DBMS classifications include relational, hierarchical and network models.
Relational systems organize data into tables.
Hierarchical systems use tree-like structures and network systems use graph-like record relationships.
Therefore option A matches the traditional three-type classification used by this question.

options.b: This is a modern classification including object-oriented and NoSQL systems, but it does not match the traditional three-type classification expected by the source.
options.c: It omits the relational model, which is one of the traditional main DBMS types.
options.d: It also omits the hierarchical and network models from the traditional classification.

questions.question: Which type of method has no implementation in the base class and must be overridden by derived classes?

correct_answer_points: An abstract method declares required behavior without providing a base implementation.
Derived/concrete classes are expected to provide the implementation.
A virtual method can have a base implementation, while static/sealed have different meanings.
Therefore Abstract method is correct.

options.a: A virtual method may have an implementation in the base class and can be overridden; it is not necessarily abstract.
options.c: A sealed method prevents further overriding in languages that support it; it does not mean the base method has no implementation.
options.d: A static method belongs to the class and is not the abstract instance-method concept described.

questions.question: Which type of adder is designed to overcome the propagation delay issues in ripple carry adders and generates the carry signal more efficiently?

correct_answer_points: A ripple-carry adder waits for carry propagation from lower bits to higher bits.
This creates propagation delay.
A look-ahead carry adder computes carry information more directly to reduce the delay.
Therefore Look-ahead carry adder is correct.

options.a: Ripple-carry adders pass carry from one stage to the next, causing propagation delay.
options.c: “Binary adder” is a general description, not the specific carry-acceleration design.
options.d: A half adder adds two bits without a carry-in and does not solve ripple-carry delay.

questions.question: Who is known as the father of AI?

correct_answer_points: John McCarthy coined the term “artificial intelligence.”
He organized the influential 1956 Dartmouth workshop.
He made foundational contributions to AI and Lisp.
Therefore John McCarthy is the expected answer.

options.a: Ada Lovelace is associated with early computing and programming, but not with being the father of AI.
options.b: Alan Turing made foundational contributions to computing and AI ideas, but John McCarthy is conventionally credited with the title.
options.d: Allen Newell was a major AI researcher, but the commonly recognized “father of AI” in this context is John McCarthy.

questions.question: Which of the following refers to the level of data abstraction that describes how data is stored?

correct_answer_points: The physical level describes how data is actually stored on storage media.
It includes low-level storage structures and access details.
The conceptual level describes the overall logical structure of the database.
Therefore Physical level is correct.

options.a: The conceptual level describes logical structure, not physical storage details.
options.c: File level is not the standard database abstraction level used for this definition.
options.d: Logical/conceptual descriptions focus on data structure and relationships rather than physical storage.

questions.question: In Python, to implement a double-ended queue, the module needs to be imported.

correct_answer_points: Python’s collections module provides deque.
deque supports efficient insertion/removal from both ends.
counter is also in collections, but “collections” is the module being imported.
Therefore collections is the correct option.

options.a: counter is a class in collections, not the module used to create a double-ended queue.
options.c: random provides random-number utilities and does not implement deque.
options.d: numpy is a numerical-computing library; deque is provided by Python’s collections module.

questions.question: A threaded binary tree is a binary tree in which:
options: (b) Each node has at most one child
(c) Each node is connected to its parent
(d) Each node has a thread connecting it to its predecessor or successor
questions.correct_answer: Each node has a thread connecting it to its predecessor or successor

correct_answer_points: Threaded binary trees use otherwise-null child pointers as threads.
Threads can point to an inorder predecessor or successor.
This supports traversal without requiring a separate stack in some implementations.
Therefore the predecessor/successor thread description is correct.

options.a: A threaded binary tree does not require every node to have two children; missing child links may become threads.
options.b: Nodes may have zero, one or two children, so “at most one child” is not the defining property.
options.c: A normal parent link is not what makes a tree threaded; threads point to traversal predecessor/successor.

questions.question: What is the full form of SQL?

correct_answer_points: SQL stands for Structured Query Language.
It is used to define, manipulate and query relational data in standard SQL systems.
The other expansions are not the accepted full form.
Therefore Structured Query Language is correct.

options.b: SQL is not officially expanded as Simple Query Language.
options.c: Systematic Query Logic is not the standard expansion.
options.d: Standard Query Level is not the standard full form.

questions.question: What is the purpose of error control in the data link layer?
options: (b) To fix errors in the physical layer

correct_answer_points: The data-link layer can detect/correct certain transmission errors depending on the protocol.
Its error-control mechanisms help deliver frames reliably over a link.
Unauthorized access and network-wide congestion are different concerns.
Therefore reliable data transmission is correct.

options.a: Unauthorized-access prevention is a security function, not the main purpose of data-link error control.
options.b: Error control detects/corrects transmission errors at the data-link level; it does not repair the physical layer itself.
options.d: Congestion management is mainly associated with network/transport mechanisms rather than data-link error control.

questions.question: Which of the following is not considered a type of e-waste?

correct_answer_points: E-waste refers to discarded electrical and electronic equipment.
Televisions, personal electronics and scanners/copiers can become e-waste.
Newspapers are ordinary paper waste, not electronic waste.
Therefore Newspapers is correct.

options.a: Televisions contain electronic components and are a common category of e-waste when discarded.
options.b: Discarded personal electronic devices are e-waste.
options.c: Scanners and copiers contain electronic/electrical components and can become e-waste.

questions.question: In which year did Intel release the first x86 microprocessor, the 8086, laying the foundation for the x86 architecture widely used in personal computers?

correct_answer_points: Intel introduced the 8086 microprocessor in 1978.
The 8086 is a 16-bit processor and is the starting point of the x86 instruction-set family used in later processors.
The Intel 4004 was introduced earlier, in 1971, so 1971 does not refer to the 8086.
Therefore 1978 is the correct release year for the 8086.

options.a: 1971 refers to Intel's 4004, the first commercial microprocessor, not the 8086.
options.b: 1981 is associated with the IBM PC era; the 8086 itself was introduced in 1978.
options.c: 1986 is later than the 8086 introduction; the processor was released in 1978.
options.d: 1991 is much later than the 8086 introduction and is not its release year.

questions.question: Which of the following describes e-Commerce?

correct_answer_points: E-commerce means conducting commercial/business activity electronically.
It can include online buying and selling of goods and services.
The broad definition therefore covers the listed activities.
Hence All of the above is the intended answer.

options.a: Doing business electronically is the core idea of e-commerce, but the question’s “all” option includes the broader listed descriptions.
options.b: “Doing business” alone is too broad because it does not specify electronic commerce.
options.c: Sale of goods can occur in e-commerce, but e-commerce also includes services and other electronic transactions.

questions.question: Frame design in the data link layer includes:
options: (a) Deciding the routing path for data packets
(b) Defining the structure of the data frame
questions.correct_answer: Defining the structure of the data frame

correct_answer_points: Data-link frame design defines the structure/format of a frame.
It includes fields such as addressing, control and error-detection information depending on the protocol.
Routing paths belong primarily to the network layer.
Therefore defining the data-frame structure is correct.

options.a: Routing determines the path between networks; frame design defines the structure of the data-link frame.
options.c: IP addressing belongs to the network layer, not frame design.
options.d: Transmission rate is a physical/link performance parameter, not the basic structural definition of a frame.

questions.question: The concept of monitors was introduced by:

correct_answer_points: C. A. R. Hoare introduced the monitor concept as a high-level synchronization mechanism.
A monitor combines shared data with procedures that control access to that data.
Only one process or thread can execute inside a monitor at a time under the classic monitor model.
Monitors simplify mutual exclusion and synchronization in concurrent programs.

options.a: Edsger Dijkstra made major contributions to concurrency, semaphores and synchronization, but the monitor concept is associated with C. A. R. Hoare.
options.b: Alan Turing was a foundational figure in theoretical computer science and computation, but he did not introduce monitors.
options.c: Tim Berners-Lee created the World Wide Web; monitors are a concurrency-control concept.
options.d: Linus Torvalds created the Linux kernel; the monitor concept predates Linux.

questions.question: Which divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm can have a worst-case time complexity of O(n²) in its basic form?

correct_answer_points: Quick sort uses divide and conquer by selecting a pivot and partitioning the array around it.
With balanced partitions, its average running time is O(n log n).
A poor pivot choice can create highly unbalanced partitions, producing O(n²) worst-case time.
Insertion sort also has O(n²) worst-case time, but it is not a divide-and-conquer algorithm.

options.b: Merge sort is a divide-and-conquer algorithm, but its worst-case time remains O(n log n) because merging each level takes linear time.
options.c: Insertion sort can have O(n²) worst-case time, but it is based on incremental insertion rather than divide and conquer.
options.d: Counting sort is a non-comparison sorting algorithm with typical complexity O(n + k), where k is the value range.

questions.question: The aliasing effect on an image can be reduced by using which of the following methods?
questions.correct_answer: Decreasing the high-frequency components of the image by blurring it

correct_answer_points: Aliasing is associated with high-frequency content being sampled inadequately.
Low-pass filtering removes/reduces high-frequency components before sampling.
Blurring acts as a low-pass operation.
Therefore decreasing high-frequency components by blurring is correct.

options.a: Sharpening increases high-frequency components, which can make aliasing artifacts more visible rather than reducing them.
options.b: Increasing high-frequency components does not suppress aliasing; it can make the sampling problem worse.
options.c: The wording says increasing high-frequency components by blurring, but blurring actually decreases high-frequency content.

questions.question: In MySQL, which type of value should not be enclosed inside quotation marks?

correct_answer_points: Numeric FLOAT values are numeric literals, not strings.
Quotation marks make a value a string literal.
DATE, VARCHAR and CHAR are commonly represented as character/date literals where quoting is required in SQL syntax.
Therefore FLOAT is the intended answer.

options.a: DATE values are commonly written as quoted date literals in SQL syntax.
options.b: VARCHAR is a character/string type, so its literal values are normally quoted.
options.d: CHAR is a character/string type, so its literal values are normally quoted.

questions.question: The term used to describe the maximum amount of data that can be transmitted over a communication channel in a given time period is:

correct_answer_points: Data rate is the amount of data transmitted per unit time.
Bandwidth can also describe channel capacity, but the wording “amount of data ... in a given time period” points to data rate.
Latency is delay, not throughput.
Therefore Data rate is correct.

options.a: Bandwidth describes the capacity of a communication channel; it is related to possible data transfer but is not exactly the measured amount per unit time in this wording.
options.c: Latency is the delay before data reaches the destination, not the amount transmitted per unit time.
options.d: A protocol is a set of communication rules, not a measure of transmission quantity.

questions.question: Which characteristics are taken together in chromaticity?

correct_answer_points: Chromaticity describes color independent of brightness/luminance.
Hue identifies the basic color family.
Saturation describes color purity/intensity.
Therefore hue and saturation are the chromaticity components.

options.b: Brightness/luminance describes intensity, not chromaticity itself.
options.c: Brightness is not part of chromaticity; chromaticity is based on hue and saturation.
options.d: Brightness is not a chromaticity component; saturation and hue are.
